st: The great stagnation between gold, bitcoin, iPhones and a rosier future

sec.t: ff.50.1 The oddness of the last 50 years
sec.p: In 2011 Tyler Cowen, an economics professor at George Mason University, published the famous book The Great Stagnation, arguing that the last 50 years have seen techno-economic stagnation. Then there's a website, WTF happened in 1971, that collects charts thrown off kilter…

sec.t: ff.50.2 Gold, silver, myrrh, beer and Bitcoin
sec.p: The golden age. Columbia economist Saifedean Ammous, in The Bitcoin Standard, points out that the technological progress of the 20th century (symbolised by the belle époque) coincided with the implementation of the gold standard, the monetary system that guaranteed the…

It's not that there's been no progress in the last 50 years. Quite the opposite. Here we try to be optimistic and positive first and foremost. But technological stagnation in some sectors is undeniable.
